title: HKMA and HKUST Launch PQC Toolkit to Accelerate Banking Sector Transition by 2030 - Quantum Computing Report
gist: The HKMA and HKUST launched a PQC Toolkit to move Hong Kong's licensed banks from an average Quantum Preparedness Index of 2.3/10 (July 2026 audit) to full readiness of 10.0 by 2030, covering cryptographic inventories (CBOMs), HNDL risk prioritization, vendor audits and board accountability tied to supervisory reviews.

insights.claim: An HKMA baseline audit in July 2026 found Hong Kong's banking sector averaged a Quantum Preparedness Index score of just 2.3 out of 10.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows a large unaddressed PQC migration workload in a major financial center.
insights.quote: revealed that Hong Kong’s banking sector averaged an initial Quantum Preparedness Index (QPI) score of just 2.3 out of 10

insights.claim: Banks in Hong Kong acknowledged the theoretical risk of cryptanalytically relevant quantum computers, but system-level migration remained at an early stage.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Awareness-execution gap implies multi-year spending ahead on discovery and migration.

insights.claim: The HKMA targets all regulated institutions reaching full quantum preparedness (QPI 10.0) by 2030.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A hard 2030 regulatory deadline creates a defined demand window for PQC vendors serving Asian banks.

insights.claim: The toolkit requires banks to inventory cryptographic assets, legacy public keys and third-party dependencies, generating Cryptographic Bills of Materials across core banking platforms.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: CBOM generation is a concrete procurement category for crypto-discovery tooling.

insights.claim: Banks are to prioritize data by confidentiality shelf-life and exposure window to mitigate 'harvest now, decrypt later' interception of transaction archives.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Long-lived financial data drives urgency independent of when quantum computers arrive.

insights.claim: Discovery processes target public-key dependencies across core transaction engines, SWIFT gateway interfaces and Hardware Security Modules.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: HSM and payment-gateway vendors face PQC upgrade cycles.

insights.claim: Quantum-safe transition audits will be integrated into HKMA's ongoing supervisory reviews, with clear executive and board accountability.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Turns PQC from voluntary best practice into supervised compliance.

insights.claim: Because banks depend on webs of third-party software for core banking, clearing and communications, the toolkit provides standardized procurement questionnaires and engagement templates to audit supplier PQC roadmaps.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Core ledger, HSM and cloud vendors selling to Hong Kong banks will need credible PQC roadmaps to win deals.

insights.claim: The toolkit will be continuously updated to reflect revisions to international standards such as NIST's finalized post-quantum parameters.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Alignment with NIST standards reduces fragmentation risk for global vendors.
